scope: Broaden the open-source peer inventory by checking OCCT's DXF/ACIS translator availability, mlightcad's exact parser/converter routes and lineage, and a narrow MIT DXF text parser.

method.kind: Primary project documentation, package metadata, and public source review
method.evidenceBoundary: Claims are limited to the cited public project documentation and package metadata. No runtime behavior, binary-DXF support, exact version fidelity, 3D geometry, or local defect is inferred without execution and generated controls.

evidence.observed: Open CASCADE's own component catalog identifies DXF and ACIS SAT/SAB exchange as OCCT extensions, and its component repository describes itself as a public preview of commercial extensions whose full components are accessed separately. CAD Assistant attributes DXF and ACIS import to commercial XDE components and restricts export/conversion for those imported models.
doesNotEstablish: that OCCT's open-source B-rep kernel is unavailable
a freely redistributable open-source OCCT SAT/SAB or DXF translator
semantic behavior of any commercial component release
evidence.planUse: Mark the vendor DXF/ACIS translators OCCT_COMMERCIAL_EXCHANGE and exclude them from open-source parser/writer votes. Keep cq-acis parser evidence and OCCT-family kernel evidence separate.

evidence.observed: RealDWG-Web documents a built-in MIT AcDbNativeDxfConverter. Its DWG converter is not registered by default; the documented open-source option uses LibreDWG. A separate DWG converter is private/proprietary, and CAD Viewer describes its open-source viewer as focused on 2D while the proprietary parser advertises partial SAB decoding for 3DSOLID.
doesNotEstablish: runtime parser correctness or release-specific capability
Binary DXF support by the default MIT converter
an independent DWG parser vote beyond LibreDWG lineage
ACIS or B-rep semantic support in the open-source viewer
evidence.planUse: Admit only the named built-in MIT DXF route as an optional pinned DXF parser/consumer check. Keep optional GPL dxf-json, LibreDWG DWG, and private DWG converter as separate route identities.

evidence.topic: mlightcad converter-family lineage and model boundary
evidence.observed: The project documents multiple DXF converters, including an optional GPL dxf-json package described as a fork, alongside the default MIT converter. Parsing into an AutoCAD-like application data model does not itself demonstrate raw record or graph preservation.
doesNotEstablish: the full ancestry of dxf-json relative to other JavaScript DXF parsers
that all converter routes have identical behavior
lossless opaque-object or writer round-trip fidelity
evidence.planUse: Record converter package, revision, and license; audit lineage before counting an independent peer; compare raw source inventory separately from normalized database-model observations.

evidence.observed: The MIT package metadata says version 1.1.2, while its GitHub release page shows no tagged releases. Its documented API parses DXF text and its README lists common 2D entities, tables, blocks/inserts, viewports, text/some MTEXT, and some XData while explicitly excluding 3DSolids and some other classes.
evidence.planUse: Keep only as an optional source-pinned LEGACY_DXF_TEXT_SUBSET comparator on locally generated ASCII controls; no dependency or test lane.

nextActions: Keep route identity and license explicit in the existing peer inventory.
Do not admit OCCT commercial translators as open-source peer evidence.
If an optional mlightcad or gds parser is already available at a composed checkpoint, use only local generated controls and report exact route/version/encoding/disposition.
Do not add any peer to the fast loop, build graph, CTest, or dependency set.
Keep J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 DEFERRED_EXTERNAL.
